answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil floods by forcing every new identity to lock a scarce on-chain relic for a long unbonding window before any reward nectar can be withdrawn. Spinning a fable of a thousand independent workers then stops being cheap: the attacker must buy or mint a thousand relics and keep that capital frozen the whole time. At a 40-token stake with a 30-day lock, one thousand fake identities cost 40,000 tokens plus opportunity cost, which typically exceeds what stuffing attestations can earn.
